title: Ruling 2026-01: Taxpayer's Conveyance of Parcels to LLC for Which it is Sole Member
text:
Date: February 23, 2026

Written by: Will S. Baker, Assistant Attorney General

Approved by: William C. Shouldice, IV, Commissioner of Taxes

This is a formal ruling for your client [Company] regarding the Vermont Property Transfer Tax treatment of a transaction described below. This ruling is based on your representations communicated in your letter dated [date] and email dated [date].

Facts 

1. Your client [Company] (“Taxpayer” herein) owns three parcels in the State of Vermont. One is a residential rental property, and the other two are adjacent parcels to be combined into a single commercial parcel. The Taxpayer is the sole owner of these three parcels.

2. Taxpayer will convey or has conveyed all three parcels to a single limited liability company. The Taxpayer is the sole member of the LLC – there are no other owners.

Discussion 

You asked whether Taxpayer’s conveyance of its parcels to an LLC for which it is the sole member would incur Vermont Property Transfer Tax. These transactions are not subject to Property Transfer Tax.

The Property Transfer Tax is a tax upon the transfer by deed or transfer of a controlling interest of property within the State. 32 V.S.A. § 9602. However, there are exceptions to the tax. One such exemption is for transfers to effectuate a mere change of form of ownership, where there is no change in beneficial ownership. 32 V.S.A. 9603(6).

In this case, the Taxpayer is the sole owner of the three parcels being transferred. The transfer is from Taxpayer to an LLC, and the Taxpayer is the sole member of the LLC. Taxpayer remains the beneficial owner of the three parcels. For this reason, there is no change in beneficial ownership and the three transfers are exempt from Property Transfer Tax.

General Provisions 

Issuance of this ruling is conditioned upon the understanding that neither the taxpayer nor a related taxpayer is currently under audit or involved in an administrative appeal or litigation concerning the subject matters of the ruling. This ruling is issued solely to the taxpayer and is limited to the facts presented, as affected by current statutes and regulations.

Other taxpayers may refer to this ruling, when redacted to protect confidentiality, to see the Department’s general approach, but the Department will not be bound by this ruling in the case of any other taxpayer or in the case of any change in the relevant statutes or regulations.

This ruling will be made public after deletion of the taxpayer’s name and any information that may identify the taxpayer. A copy of this ruling showing the proposed deletions is attached, and you may request within 30 days that the Commissioner delete any further information that might identify the taxpayer. The final discretion as to deletions rests with the Commissioner.

You have the right to appeal this ruling within 30 days. 3 V.S.A. §§ 808, 815.
